chapter: Photographs: Eddie Miller, Shields and Willow band
title: Photos with Eddie Miller and Fazola at the Front Dance
summary: Sal shows pictures and recalls playing with Eddie Miller and Fazola at the dance hall, and who played better on which instrument.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I'm going to mention Lester Nelson. I have a few pictures here. Temple Black. Temple Black is his name.
Here's a picture here. Eddie Miller and I. I don't know.
I don't know. I don't know. I don't know.
At the Roseville. Yeah, we just met up again.

Yeah, we were playing a little get-together up there, you know. A fun, free job, you know, and I just playing tenor. And then I got up there, I was playing a little play. I was playing a little play. I was playing a little play. I was playing a little play. I was playing a little play. I was telling Eddie sometimes to come back in a speech. I'm talking to Eddie and snap the pictures.
Did you work with him much?
Eddie at the front, yeah. At the front, yeah. At the front, mm-hmm. Yeah, I was passionate to get married, Eddie, man.

He's playing a lot. At the gym hotel, he's playing a sound when he saw him. Eddie Miller. I got Eddie Miller and Fazz Ola, the first job I ever had at the front dance on both of them. And Eddie played better. In those days, Eddie played better clarinet than Fazz. And Fazz played better, I mean, and Eddie played better tenor than Fazz. So he swapped around, see. And we had Eddie Miller and Fazz at the same time in the front, see. And we had a good kick in the back, man. Wasn't Bill Bourgeois in there at one time, too? Well, Bourgeois played that before then. Oh, he was there before then. Before these five. Well, Bill could play better than them at the time.
We sent those pictures of Howard Jacob was supposed to use them in the paper, and then I think somebody sent it. That's what you want to see. Less than nothing.
